question: It is given that the graph of $y=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$ (where $a,b,c,d$ are real) has at least $3$ points of intersection with the $x$-axis. Prove that either there are exactly $4$ distinct points of intersection, or one of those $3$ points of intersection is a local minimum or maximum.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
